items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Came Christmas and the New Year of 1945, and John Kirby contacted me for a gig.

ctx.x: The next night Eddie did the number again, which was a number he did in his attraction set and he missed in the passage at the same place again and that did bug him, because it was a number he had played many times and had never missed a note before, and I suppose many others that witnessed this incident really felt sorry for Eddie and he became very upset because he had the passage two consecutive nights. The third one it was the same, and we all knew that now he was fighting with the passage and that's what he…

We worked at the Uptown for one month and left for a two months engagement in Chicago, at the Ambassador East Hotel which was one of the finest hotels in the city. We were to play in the Pump Room where only one other Negro orchestra had ever played and that was John Kirby's "biggest" little band in the world. I had heard many of their broadcasts and had never before heard six instruments that sounded like ten. Kirby's band had played in many places where Negro musicians had never played before and the "Pump…

Teddy engaged his favourite drummer J.C. Heard, who had been a member of Teddy's big band, and added George James on baritone. This made the front line four horns, trumpet, trombone, clarinet and baritone sax. The baritone gave the band a heavy sound and the arrangement that Teddy made along with some that he had arranged made us sound quite big also.
